comparator.name: Communication and Information Studies
comparator.sourceNotes: This example follows the curriculum for September 2026 entrants. It includes Humane AI and Digital Society as the first-year elective, its second-year project course and a 30 EC minor. The regular pathway is taught in English, including the thesis. Groningen also offers a Dutch track.

components.name: Materiality of Communication
components.note: Studies how media and physical forms shape communication.

components.name: Changing Minds: Persuasion and Argumentation
components.note: Studies how persuasion and arguments influence attitudes.

components.name: Essential Skills for Academics
components.note: Builds academic skills for studying communication.

components.name: Intercultural Communication
components.note: Studies communication across cultural contexts.

components.name: Observing Communication in the Wild: Qualitative Methods
components.note: Develops qualitative research skills for studying communication.

components.name: Text and Cognition
components.note: Studies how readers process and interpret texts.

components.name: Language in Interaction
components.note: Studies how people use language in interaction.

components.name: Humane AI in Digital Societies: Introduction
components.note: One of the two first-year faculty-wide choices.

components.name: Corporate and Workplace Communication
components.note: Studies communication in organizations and workplaces.

components.name: Analysing Communication: Quantitative Approaches
components.note: Develops quantitative approaches to communication research.

components.name: Social Media Discourses and Affordances
components.note: Studies discourse and how platform features shape interaction.

components.name: Statistics
components.note: Develops statistical analysis for communication research.

components.name: Design and Evaluation
components.note: Designs and evaluates communication interventions.

components.name: Health Communication
components.note: Studies communication in health contexts.

components.name: Language in Context
components.note: Studies language in its context of use.

components.name: Humane AI in Digital Societies: Projects
components.note: One of four faculty-wide choices. This example continues the first-year Humane AI theme.

components.name: Minor
components.note: Approved minor space totaling 30 EC.

components.name: Communication and Societal Change
components.note: Studies communication in relation to social change.

components.name: Literacy in Society
components.note: Studies literacy practices and their place in society.

components.name: CIS Bachelor Thesis and Research Seminar
components.note: A supervised research seminar and thesis, normally written in English on this pathway.

components.name: CIS Case Study
components.note: Applies communication study to an integrated case.

comparatorRouteSelection.basis: The unqualified degree target follows the regular English-taught pathway. The Dutch track has specified Dutch-language seminars, assessments and thesis. The 2026 entry regulations list two first-year electives. This example uses the first listed, Humane AI and Digital Society. The second-year project course continues that theme from among the four faculty-wide choices.

alternativeSelection.assessment: Three complete plans meet course feasibility and distinctness. Their separate emphases are communication and media analysis, workplace and health settings, and digitally mediated communication and AI.

comparisonAlignment.rationale: Both study how arguments and persuasive choices shape a message. UCR focuses on rhetoric, public speaking and written argument.
Both examine how language works in interaction. UCR studies turn-taking and dialogue within a broader course on stylistics.
Both address cognitive aspects of language. UCR studies reading and comprehension alongside spoken language and language disorders.
Both study how the material form of a medium shapes communication. UCR traces the technologies and artifacts of media history.
Groningen studies social-media discourse and platform features. UCR examines storytelling and representation across older and newer media.
Groningen studies communication and societal change. UCR courses explore specific examples such as climate communication and racial representation.
Both examine communication in organizations. UCR focuses on leadership, storytelling and persuasion.
Both examine communication in health care. UCR studies consultation and shared decisions within a wider health psychology course.
Groningen has a dedicated intercultural communication course. UCR studies culture and identity across sociology, rhetoric and leadership.
Groningen studies language in context. UCR approaches context through stylistics and social theory.
Both develop academic skills. UCR includes source evaluation, research questions and academic writing.
Both use qualitative research to investigate social meaning. UCR covers interviews, observation and interpretation across a range of social questions.
Both develop statistical analysis. UCR combines statistics with experimental methods and examples from psychology.
Groningen applies quantitative methods specifically to communication. UCR applies these methods in psychology and market research.
Groningen has a dedicated design and evaluation course for communication. UCR offers broader study in research design and measurement.
Groningen’s faculty elective links AI with digital society. UCR explores AI ethics and technical AI methods in separate courses.
Groningen continues its faculty-wide AI theme through a project course. UCR offers separate work in AI ethics, media and data.
Groningen reserves 30 EC for an approved minor.
Groningen studies literacy as a social practice in a dedicated course.
Groningen requires a 10 EC thesis and research seminar. UCR’s optional research element sits outside its degree schedule.
Groningen has a dedicated 10 EC communication case study.

This curriculum applies to students starting at Groningen in September 2026.

audience.programmeDescription: Study how people use language, images and media to make meaning and influence others. The regular Groningen pathway is taught in English. A Dutch track is also available.
audience.comparisonExplanation: Groningen combines communication analysis, practical applications and research. The UCR options emphasize discourse and media, workplace and health communication, or digital media and AI.

cellNotes.text: Both study how arguments and persuasive choices shape a message. UCR focuses on rhetoric, public speaking and written argument.
Both examine how language works in interaction. UCR studies turn-taking and dialogue within a broader course on stylistics.
Both address cognitive aspects of language. UCR studies reading and comprehension alongside spoken language and language disorders.
Both study how the material form of a medium shapes communication. UCR traces the technologies and artifacts of media history.
Groningen studies social-media discourse and platform features. UCR examines storytelling and representation across older and newer media.
Groningen studies communication and societal change. UCR courses explore specific examples such as climate communication and racial representation.
Both examine communication in organizations. UCR focuses on leadership, storytelling and persuasion.
Both examine communication in health care. UCR studies consultation and shared decisions within a wider health psychology course.
Groningen has a dedicated intercultural communication course. UCR studies culture and identity across sociology, rhetoric and leadership.
Groningen studies language in context. UCR approaches context through stylistics and social theory.
Both develop academic skills. UCR includes source evaluation, research questions and academic writing.
Both use qualitative research to investigate social meaning. UCR covers interviews, observation and interpretation across a range of social questions.
Both develop statistical analysis. UCR combines statistics with experimental methods and examples from psychology.
Groningen applies quantitative methods specifically to communication. UCR applies these methods in psychology and market research.
Groningen has a dedicated design and evaluation course for communication. UCR offers broader study in research design and measurement.
Groningen’s faculty elective links AI with digital society. UCR explores AI ethics and technical AI methods in separate courses.
Groningen continues its faculty-wide AI theme through a project course. UCR offers separate work in AI ethics, media and data.
Groningen reserves 30 EC for an approved minor.
Groningen studies literacy as a social practice in a dedicated course.
Groningen requires a 10 EC thesis and research seminar. UCR’s optional research element sits outside its degree schedule.
Groningen has a dedicated 10 EC communication case study.
